record_notes.DCP-LETT-1055: 21st with supplied January 1847. Naturalists almanack received, new to Darwin, improvements suggested for equation of time, conversion tables, magnification and monthly weather. Requests table rather than rules; suggestions not implemented contents. Hopes another year although later Jenyns letter says publication stopped after 1847. That retrospective letter to Francis is a different voice and time, not Darwin current knowledge or incoming cover.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1125: October 8, supplied 1847. Coloured map received and coral chapters carefully read, but no copy yet obtained for complete reading of Jukes work. Lyell agreement and Crawfurd ethnographic praise are oral reports, not independent full incoming text. Darwin welcomes support while calling own coral work bold/speculative; unvisited Barrier–New Caledonia reefs remain desired investigation. Do not mark the whole book read.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1165: March 25, supplied 1848 from Mallet/Herschel connections. Answers missing Ball enquiry, cannot identify enclosed or described hook and offers limited remembered fishing/food observations. His generalization about not hearing other examples is limited knowledge, not a universal fact. Space-for-specimens suggestion is explicitly Ball idea sent via Mallet, not Mallet original idea as summary implies. Forwarded to Herschel and hopes for Admiralty action; action not confirmed. Collection/cataloguing motive is editorial possibility.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1569: May 5, supplied 1847 from Kolbe return and Bunsen geology. Sends specimen parcel through Kolbe, larger than expected; missed Kolbe visit discovered only after returning home. Hopes visitor had other business, does not know. Later Bunsen 1851/1853 analyses and acknowledgment cannot become current receipt or results. Arrangement that Kolbe would carry parcel may have been oral or missing note.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1072: March 20, supplied 1847. Cover addresses Gustav von Leonhard while respectful tone suggests Darwin may mean father Karl Cäsar; keep recipient authority and possible mental confusion separate. Review of Volcanic Islands not found; later South America review is different work. Publisher instructed to send South America, not proved delivered. No source-complete incoming review/letter.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1269: November 12, 1849. Lovén paper now read, following earlier translation request to Mary Lyell. Alepas squalicola specimen still requested, confident new-genus claim precedes examination; offers Lovén suggested name but no later evidence name came from him. Park Street is parcel address; Down for letters, not physical relocation. Exact Lovén address unknown, enclosed via Forchhammer. Preserved November 15 Forchhammer 1270 is later and cannot be this knowledge input. Later Steenstrup specimens and revised rank/name are future, not current material.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1041: Wednesday evening letter continued Thursday morning within December 1848–1849 interval. P1 lost brown-paper-covered volume low priority, identification unknown. Closing and Thursday marker share P2; marker starts a later section and P3 acknowledges Sir John cheque. Do not make cheque knowledge available to Wednesday section. Receipt and completed microscope will be sent later; instrument not yet complete. Harriet addressee distinct from father John and son John. Shared period with 1212 does not establish same Wednesday.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1224: February 10, supplied 1849. Missing Philippi information identifies Alepas at Berlin, asks Müller loan/dissection permission and other specimens from Sicily/Mediterranean. Almost all genera examined except Alepas, future requests not available specimens. Park Street routing and ambassador Christian Bunsen separate from Robert Bunsen geologist. Later monograph implies Alepas loan but gives no current delivery; dubious Anatifa villosa and absent Sicilian specimens not facts resolved here. No preserved Philippi or Müller direct input.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1318: April 3, 1850 Masters incoming, full surviving source. Explicit reply to missing Darwin pea/bean pollination question; reports cultivar variation and stronger neighboring Brassica cross-pollination, with stated Knight marrow origin and anecdotes. Attribute observations and clouds-of-pollen account to Masters, not Darwin or modern verified botany. Undated Darwin crosses/ink note/Gärtner comparison are separate later layers; literal 659 reference conflicts with extent of owned 1844 edition and editorial suggested 104–107 is not manuscript text. Later Variation citations do not establish 1850 reading date. No preserved question, later Darwin response or dated knowledge witness located.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-13775: October 2, questioned 1847 from possible December account transaction, with February 1848 similar entry also known. Requests six bottles each two ounces with corks, not sixty-two ounces. Original order a week or ten days earlier apparently overlooked; no new delivery or payment proved. Baxter father versus later son succession matters to identity and loose chronology. Do not date receipt to later account entry or claim questioned year secure.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1120: 20th assigned September 1847 from London expense September 18. Memoir found during London trip after previous collection attempt failed because porter absent; exact receipt/read day not specified. Read private 1847 version, not future 1849 journal version. Rejects detrital barriers yet newly more receptive to ice-lake possibility after Glen Glastig outlet evidence, explicitly not yet believer. Scotsman submission planned and copy conditional on publication; Lyell advice oral, Milne cover note missing. South America fjord analogy offered as possible relevance, not completed proof.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-560: Fresh full February 20, 1840 context, formerly misdated March in old editions. Missing Milne enquiry about earthquake coincidences answered: high frequency makes chance overlap likely, no own intercontinental correlation record. Untraced L’Institut memory and possible later editorial alternative remain uncertain. Paper publication/copy promised, not delivered here. Weather, water and moon hypotheses carefully distinguished; Calabria/Scotland report intriguing, not established causal link. Not current 1847 Glen Roy incoming evidence.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-562F: Fresh full March 28, 1840 Milne incoming. After professional delay read Darwin volcanic paper twice; argues lithology controls propagation and discusses weather/water hypotheses. Explicit thanks for caution about coincident earthquakes identifies reply to 560, already accepted in earlier batch 15. Witness accounts of steam/flame and Daubeny suggestion are attributed reports; no independent Darwin observation. Neither composition nor later citation proves Darwin receipt. Different subject/time from 1120.
